A1: Approach motions (LP1, LP4) end with a vertical descent, so a blocked approach (obstruction) loads the wrist from below.
A2: No part is held while approaching the grasp position (LP1); a part is held in LP2-LP5.
A3: A class named only 'collision' does not fix the side of contact: any side is possible, including the side of a more specific class of the same problem.
A4: Contact on the carried part acts at a longer moment arm from the wrist sensor than contact on the tool, so the torque-to-force ratio tells the two apart.
A5: 'moved' and 'slightly_moved' (LP3) describe the same physical change, a shift of the part in the gripper, at different magnitudes.
A6: Collisions are impacts (force rises, then decays within the window); obstructions block the motion (force persists or grows); a changed payload is a static change.
